paper_metadata.title: Extent of neocortical resection and surgical outcome of epilepsy: Intracranial EEG analysis

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a consecutive sample of 177 patients with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria (neocortical onset, excluding hippocampal sclerosis). Baseline characteristics and recruitment settings are well-described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: consecutive patients who had undergone resective epilepsy surgery and intracranial EEG monitoring with subdural electrodes for intractable localization-related epilepsy between 1995 and 2003.
items.reasoning: The population is clearly defined as patients with intractable localization-related epilepsy requiring intracranial monitoring.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We retrospectively reviewed the records of consecutive patients who had undergone resective epilepsy surgery and intracranial EEG monitoring
items.reasoning: The use of consecutive patients from a specific surgical program minimizes selection bias compared to convenience sampling.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between 1995 and 2003.
items.reasoning: The specific years of recruitment are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Seoul National University Hospital, 28, Yongkeun dong, Chongno Ku, Seoul, 110-744, Korea.
items.reasoning: The specific tertiary care center and location are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We included only patients who had neocortical ictal onsets, and, therefore, excluded patients with radiologic evidence of hippocampal sclerosis or mesial temporal ictal onsets
items.reasoning: Specific clinical and radiological criteria for inclusion and exclusion are stated.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: One hundred seventy-seven patients were included in the study
items.reasoning: The study includes a large consecutive cohort; only two patients were excluded from surgery due to clinical reasons (eloquent area/multifocality), which is standard for this population.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The median age at epilepsy onset was 12.5 years (range 0.25–36 years). The median age at surgery was 27.9 years (range 11–51 years). The median latency between epilepsy onset and epilepsy surgery was 15.4 years (range 1–50 years).
items.reasoning: Key demographics and clinical history (age, onset, duration) are provided.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: All patients had at least 2 years of follow-up, and the median follow-up was over 8 years. There was no significant difference in follow-up duration between outcome groups.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: All the patients had been followed for more than 2 years... The average follow-up period was 8.24 years (range 2–15 years).
items.reasoning: The study reports on the full cohort of 177 patients with long-term follow-up.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text does not explicitly mention dropouts or attempts to contact them, likely because the cohort was restricted to those with >2 years follow-up.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Reasons for any potential loss to follow-up prior to the 2-year mark are not discussed.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No data provided on patients who did not meet the 2-year follow-up inclusion threshold.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: There was no significant difference in the follow-up period between the class I (seizure-free) group (8.09 years) and the class II–IV group (8.33 years).
items.reasoning: The authors confirmed that follow-up duration was balanced across outcome groups, reducing the risk of attrition bias.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (EEG features and resection extent) were measured using standardized digital systems and clearly defined criteria for ictal onset, propagation, and interictal abnormalities.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Ictal onset was defined as a paroxysmal sustained rhythmic EEG change differentiated from the background EEG and interictal waves... We classified the ictal-onset zone by location (temporal or extratemporal) and distribution (focal, regional, or widespread).
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors (EEG patterns) are defined with specific electrographic criteria.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Intracranial EEG recordings of the patients were made with a 128-channel Telefactor Beehive Horizon digital video monitoring system.
items.reasoning: Standardized, high-resolution digital equipment was used for measurement.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: We grossly divided the patients into three groups according to the extent of resection based on ictal onset and spreading ictal rhythm: group I... group II... group III
items.reasoning: The 3-second and 5-second cut-offs for resection extent appear somewhat arbitrary/data-driven, though they are clearly defined.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All the patients... had undergone a presurgical evaluation that included MRI, postoperative pathologic evaluation, scalp and intracranial video-EEG monitoring
items.reasoning: The protocol for intracranial monitoring was consistent across the cohort.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: We reviewed various intracranial EEG findings and resection extent... in 177 consecutive patients
items.reasoning: The study reports complete EEG and resection data for the entire analyzed sample.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Missing data handling is not mentioned, suggesting a complete-case analysis.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) was measured using the internationally recognized Engel classification with a minimum 2-year follow-up, which is the clinical standard.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Surgical outcomes were classified according to the method of Engel and colleagues (Engel et al., 1993).
items.reasoning: The Engel scale is a well-validated and standard measure for epilepsy surgery outcomes.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: All the patients had been followed for more than 2 years... average follow-up period was 8.24 years
items.reasoning: Long-term follow-up and use of a standardized scale ensure reliability.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Surgical outcomes were classified according to the method of Engel and colleagues
items.reasoning: The same classification system was applied to all patients.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.
